name: Fort Worth
lead: First Rule Boxing Club is based right here in north Fort Worth, off Harmon Rd near the Alliance corridor. Group boxing, youth classes, and personal training — all coached, all in one gym.
body: We're tucked into the Harmon Rd corridor in north Fort Worth, a quick pull off I-35W for members coming from Alliance, Northlake, and the neighborhoods around Eagle Mountain Lake. It's a working gym, not a big-box fitness floor — heavy bags, mitts, a coached class schedule, and an owner who knows your name by week two.

Most members start the same way: a group class to learn the basics, build some conditioning, and see if boxing is actually for them. From there it's wherever you want to take it — stick with group classes, add 1-on-1 coaching, or just use open gym time to put in extra rounds on your own.

We run two training windows Monday through Thursday — an early block before the workday starts and an evening block after it ends — so Fort Worth members training around a 9-to-5 or school pickup still have a real way to make class.

Whether you've never thrown a punch or you boxed years ago and want back in the gym, the first step is the same: show up to a class, meet the coach, and see what the room feels like. That's the only way to know if it's a fit.

name: Keller
lead: First Rule Boxing Club trains members from Keller, TX — a short drive up Hwy 377 or I-35W to our north Fort Worth gym for group boxing, youth classes, and personal training.
body: A good share of our roster drives in from Keller — close enough that it's a normal part of a weekday routine, not a special trip. Keller families in particular tend to land in our youth boxing program, looking for a structured, coached activity that builds discipline alongside the fitness.

For Keller adults, group boxing classes are the usual starting point — a 45-minute class that covers technique, pad work, and conditioning without requiring any prior experience. From there, some members move into 1-on-1 coaching when they want more individual attention on technique.

Our schedule is built around two training windows Monday through Thursday, early morning and evening, so Keller members commuting toward Fort Worth or working locally can still make class before or after work.
If you're in Keller and curious whether boxing's a fit — for yourself or your kid — the best next step is just showing up to a class. No contract required to try it.
